statement: Zero production work of a simulation advances after simulate() returns. The UnifiedRebalancer's rebalance-check reconcile queue owns a current-work completion contract - isCurrentWorkIdle() and awaitCurrentWorkIdle(), idle iff draining is false, pending is empty and inFlight is empty - and the rebalancer delegates to it; future work (retry instants, exhausted items, the periodic cadence) stays the timer owner's. The simulator consumes that contract as one more explicit owner in the same instant-closure fixpoint as Raft and the gateway, never by inspecting queue internals and never by a bounded settle loop, so a scenario cannot return with an admitted rebalance check still executing and hand its continuations to the next generation.

constraints.statement: No second pending-work tracker. OwnerKeyReconcileQueue already maintains draining, pending and inFlight across the real reconcile lifetime; the contract is expressed from those three and from nothing else - not timers, host turns or promise counts.
Idle means every item already admitted has completed or moved into an explicitly future-owned state. It does not mean the rebalancer will never work again, and it never waits for a retry deadline.
The simulator consumes awaitCurrentWorkIdle() only. pending, inFlight and draining stay queue-owner internals, and the harness never discovers queues by crawling.

Rebalancer owners join the same explicit-owner closure set as Raft and the gateway, because a rebalancer continuation may create gateway or Raft work at the same instant. No appended Promise.all after closure and no new bounded settle(N).

Attribution implementation, generation-root isolation, UUID injection, lineage retention, scheduler and PCT, current-instant ordering, owner calibration means, priority partition ordering, the AVAILABLE/AUTHORITATIVE split, rebalancer semantics and future retry cadence are unchanged. No extra host turns in simulate(), no sleeps, no warm-up runs, no transcript tolerance, no simulation-only queue drain.
